name: Axiom Systems Ferrofluid Projector FP-3 'Tar Pit'
description:
A weapon that fires pressurized streams of magnetically-responsive ferrofluid that adheres to surfaces and can be remotely activated to form rigid structures, constrict around targets, or generate localized magnetic fields. The Tar Pit turns a liquid weapon into a controllable solid on command.

Axiom Systems designed the FP-3 as a non-lethal capture weapon. The ferrofluid stream coats a target in a thin layer of magnetic liquid that, when activated by the weapon's remote signal, transitions from liquid to a rigid lattice that immobilizes limbs, seals airways, and locks joints. The activation is selective — the operator chooses which portions of the ferrofluid to harden and which to leave liquid, allowing precise control over the degree of immobilization.

The Tar Pit's lethal potential comes from its ability to seal airways and restrict circulation. A full-body ferrofluid coating that is activated simultaneously creates a rigid shell that prevents breathing, and the magnetic lattice can be tightened to restrict blood flow. Axiom classifies the weapon as non-lethal, but the line between immobilization and suffocation is a matter of operator intent.
legality: Non-lethal classification — licensed for law enforcement and security
specifications:
caliber: N/A — pressurized ferrofluid stream
effective_range: 5-25 meters
rate_of_fire: Continuous stream, 3-second coating per target
capacity: 6 full-body coatings per reservoir
weight: 8.2 kg loaded
power_source: Magnetic activation transmitter, integrated battery, 4 hours
tactical_use: The Tar Pit is deployed for live capture operations where targets must be taken alive and undamaged. The ferrofluid coating immobilizes without bruising, fracturing, or causing wound trauma — making it the preferred tool for corporate extractions where the target's value depends on their physical condition. The weapon is also used for area denial — ferrofluid sprayed on floors and walls can be activated to create adhesive surfaces that trap anyone who contacts them.
cultural_context: The Ferrofluid Projector has generated debate about the definition of non-lethal force. Rights organizations point to documented suffocation deaths from over-application and argue that a weapon capable of killing through operator discretion cannot be classified as non-lethal. Axiom's defense is that any tool can be misused — a position that rings hollow when their marketing materials describe the weapon's ability to 'seal all movement, including respiratory.'
story_hooks: A target was captured using a Tar Pit and delivered to their employer — but the ferrofluid coating was never fully deactivated. The residual magnetic lattice is slowly constricting, and the removal procedure risks triggering a full activation that would crush the victim.

Someone has introduced a corrosive compound into Axiom's ferrofluid supply chain. The contaminated fluid dissolves organic tissue on contact rather than immobilizing it. Several 'non-lethal' engagements have resulted in chemical burns and tissue destruction.

physical_description.visual_profile: A bulbous, organic-looking projector with a pronounced nozzle assembly. The weapon resembles a hybrid between a caulking gun and a medical nebulizer — smooth, almost biological curves interrupted by sharp magnetic coil housings. The silhouette is asymmetrical, weighted toward the reservoir chamber.
physical_description.dimensions: 62 cm long, 18 cm wide at the widest point (reservoir bulge), 14 cm tall. Nozzle protrudes 8 cm from the main body.
physical_description.weight_description: Hefty and front-heavy when loaded (8.2 kg). The weight distribution favors the reservoir — requires two-handed grip for sustained firing. Balanced at the trigger guard, but the ferrofluid payload makes it feel like it wants to tip forward.
physical_description.primary_material: Aerospace-grade polymer frame with embedded magnetic coil housings. Nozzle assembly is reinforced titanium-steel composite to withstand ferrofluid pressure cycles.
physical_description.finish: Matte charcoal polymer body with brushed gunmetal accents around the magnetic housing. The reservoir chamber has a subtle iridescent sheen — visible ferrofluid moving beneath translucent viewport panels catches light like oil on water.
physical_description.color_scheme: Charcoal gray primary with gunmetal silver magnetic coil rings. The ferrofluid visible through viewport windows appears as a deep, shifting black-bronze liquid.
physical_description.grip_texture: Rubberized non-slip polymer with embedded texture grips. The grip wraps around the trigger guard with raised ridges for two-handed purchase. Cool to the touch due to thermal regulation of the ferrofluid reservoir.
distinctive_features: Four stacked magnetic coil rings mounted vertically along the barrel assembly — visibly humming with barely-contained energy
Transparent polycarbonate viewport panels on the reservoir bulge — shows ferrofluid level and movement
Twin pressure gauges flanking the nozzle — one for fluid pressure, one for magnetic field strength
Remote activation transmitter mounted on top rail — compact, with a small LCD display showing target lock status
Heat vents along the magnetic housing — fine mesh grilles releasing faint thermal shimmer during operation
Weapon serial plate etched into the grip safety — Axiom Systems logo prominent
Ferrofluid splatter patterns around the nozzle lip — residual traces of previous firings create dark staining
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: AXIOM SYSTEMS logo embossed on the upper receiver in silver-etched lettering. Serial number and 'NON-LETHAL CLASSIFICATION' stamp on a brass plate riveted to the left side of the reservoir. Pressure warnings in three languages stamped near the nozzle.
physical_description.condition_typical: Well-maintained by professional operators, but showing field wear. Ferrofluid residue around the nozzle is expected. Magnetic housing may show minor scoring from coil activation cycles. For Tier 3+ users, the weapon appears functional and cared-for — corporate contractors maintain these as precision tools.
